answer: A proposed lotus market rejects earning keys until 12 fresh private coding tasks pass hidden tests; each extra alias owes 12 unpaid completions. The vault verifies approved customer signatures, assigns each distinct task to one key, runs the tests and spends each task ID once. A falcon agent cannot reuse a receipt across keys; 10 aliases need 120 accepted tasks. Sampling diverse codebases and withholding tests curb canned outputs. Honest task issuers and sound tests are necessary; reusable tools and collusion can still reduce real effort.
